_meta.what: THE TEST REGISTRY for knowledge/addon-dev/ — the id ⇄ ns.Test{} ⇄ run-row join, keyed by a stable id. It is NOT where an unknown is first written down: that is a MARKER on the claim itself, in the topic file (`[gap]` / `[unverified]` / `@verify-ingame`), because an agent reading the file meets the marker in the prose it is already reading. A question earns a row here when somebody decides to TEST it. Rows also exist for questions nobody is testing (`parked`, `not-answerable`) where the reasoning was worth keeping — but the absence of a row never means an unknown was lost.
_meta.why_here: knowledge/addon-dev/ is firewalled from the game KB (its README §0), so its `@verify-ingame` markers are written inside backticks and `wowkb.gen_verify` ignores them — a DECISION, not a bug (addon-dev/README.md §6, gen_verify.py's docstring). Nothing harvests them, and nothing needs to: the marker is met at the point of USE, by whoever is about to build on the claim. This file exists for the half a marker cannot do — binding a question to the Lua that tests it and the run row that answers it. Indexed from addon-dev/README.md §1.2 as the fourth queue.
_meta.id_is_the_key: The join column between this file, the `id` on each ns.Test{} in ClientLab/T_*.lua, and each row of the `runs` capture stream (`ClientLabDB.captures.runs`, read by `wowkb.capture clab runs` / `wowkb.lab show`). An id survives the anchor line moving; anchor text does not.
_meta.expect_never_ships: `expect` lives HERE and is never compared in-game. cdmp asserts a known answer against regression; the lab discovers an unknown one, so the reader renders result beside expect and a HUMAN decides. An automatic PASS/FAIL would be the instrument grading its own subject.

status.answered: flown, read beside `expect` by a human, and drained into the KB. Carries an `answered` block naming the run, the addon version and the OBS-nnn that carried it. ITS TEST IS DELETED — in the same edit that writes the claim, exactly as house rule 2 kills probe code once its finding lands. The row survives forever and is the recipe if a patch ever makes the question worth re-asking; the Lua does not, because nothing re-checks it (`show` prints no verdict by design and `drain` refuses an answered question), so a retained test only costs run time on every pull.
status.built: a ns.Test{} with this id exists in ClientLab/ and flies on the next login/pull — Autorun runs every built test unprompted, so writing the test IS queuing it. The claim it answers carries `@pending-test: <id>` in its topic file. If it has been flown but NOT drained, a `note` says why — an undrained flown question must never look the same as an unflown one.
status.parked: a question somebody wrote out but nobody is testing. No test, no clock, no cap, no release gate. `blocked_on` says what it would take (null = nothing, it has simply not come up). The trigger for building a test is USE — someone needs the answer to write code — never age. ⚠ A row here is not required for an unknown to be recorded: the marker on the claim is, and a bare marker with no row is a perfectly good parked question.
status.not-answerable: no instrument can settle it and the reason is recorded in `expect`, so it is not re-attempted. `blocked_on` may still name what a DIFFERENT instrument would need — a desktop file read is not a ClientLab job, but it is not nothing either.

_meta.cross_check: `wowkb.lab deploy` asserts every `built` id here has a ns.Test{} and every ns.Test{} id is a `built` question. An unmatched id is a loud error, never a silent skip. An `answered` id still present in the Lua fails BY NAME — that is the direction the suite grows back in, and it is the one worth naming.
_meta.counts_as_of: 2026-08-11: 61 answered, 1 built, 27 parked, 3 not-answerable (total 92). Seven pre-12.1 probes were returned to parked when their automatic runner tainted the secure Cooldown Viewer during login; their question recipes remain here, but their executable probes were deleted. The focused AuraContainer and GetSpellCharges questions were answered and their one-shot probes deleted after the findings landed; one visual Conflagrate charge-context probe is queued.
_meta.anchor_form: <file under knowledge/addon-dev/>:<line>. `also` lists further anchors that ask the same question — one test, several places in the KB to edit when it is answered.
_meta.anchor_drift: Anchors are `<file>:<line>` and LINE NUMBERS MOVE — the KB cleanup of 2026-08-05 silently drifted several. The `id` is the durable key; an anchor is a convenience. Treat a stale anchor as a lint finding, not as evidence the question is gone. ⚠ Nothing validates anchors today; that check belongs in `wowkb.lab deploy --check`.
_meta.note_field: Free text on a question that has been flown but not drained, or is otherwise not in the state its `status` alone suggests. It exists so 'we looked and chose not to' is distinguishable from 'nobody has looked'.
_meta.evidence_classes: A row on the `runs` stream carries `source`: "measured" (an instrument read it) or "eyeball" (a human answered after being shown a stimulus by ns.Ask). They are NOT interchangeable. An eyeball verdict is the only evidence that can close a question with no programmatic oracle, and the WRONG evidence for anything measurable — so `wowkb.lab show` renders it differently and `wowkb.lab drain` requires it for a visual question and labels it loudly in the observation it mints.
_meta.blocked_on: What the question is waiting on, as a CAPABILITY rather than a task: many rows share one blocker, and `wowkb.lab blocked` groups them so the residue reads as a handful of missing capabilities instead of a pile of stuck questions. `null` means nothing is missing. Two blockers need their jargon spelled out: 'a generator that writes sibling addons' — ClientLab cannot test its own .toc from inside its own .toc without breaking itself, so every container question needs N generated throwaway addons, one per .toc variant (unbuilt, and not worth building until a .toc problem actually bites); and 'XML authoring in the lab' — the lab ships Lua only, so nothing can currently exercise the XML compiler.
_meta.two_things_that_may_never_accumulate: A MEASURED ANSWER NOT YET IN THE KB — gated by `wowkb.obs check` (14 days / 12 open), the failure that once stranded 15 answers for 12 days. And AN UNVERIFIED CLAIM SILENTLY RELIED UPON — gated by nothing mechanical, by design: the marker sits on the claim, so anyone reading the claim reads the marker, and the rule is ASK rather than assume. Everything else — parked questions, [gap] annotations — may pile up harmlessly. They are a CATALOGUE, not a backlog.
_meta.marker_lifecycle: The state of a question lives in the TOPIC FILE, on the claim: `[gap]`/`[unverified]`/`@verify-ingame` = open, nobody is on it. `@pending-test: <id>` = a ns.Test{} exists in ClientLab and will fly on the next login/pull — the id names the row here. `[client YYYY-MM-DD]` = measured and drained, marker gone. Promotion to `@pending-test` and the final rewrite are hand edits, in context, because README §7.1 wants the CLAIM rewritten rather than annotated — no tool edits prose.
_meta.shrinking: THE SUITE SHRINKS AS THE KB GROWS, and that is the intended shape. Answering a question moves it out of ClientLab and into a topic file: 32 answered questions were swept out at once when this rule was adopted, taking the suite from 57 ids to 25 and deleting T_Module.lua and T_CooldownManager.lua entirely. A lab that only accumulates is re-measuring settled facts during a pull.

questions.question: Is a nested-`.toc` library (LibStub) enumerated by the client as an addon in its own right? And is a plainly-installed top-level addon (RaiderIO) reported as existing even though it is missing from AddOns.txt?
questions.expect: DoesAddOnExist("LibStub") == false and DoesAddOnExist("RaiderIO") == true. That combination confirms the §19b folder-name rule AND kills the draft's inference that absence from AddOns.txt proves never-enumerated. Either half coming back the other way rewrites §1.

questions.question: Does the addon sandbox expose `require`, `os` or `io`?
questions.expect: All three nil. 2298 shipped .lua files contain zero uses of require/dofile/loadfile/module/os./io., which is corroboration by absence; this converts it to a measurement. A non-nil `os` would be a notable finding worth its own KB section.

questions.question: Is `string.rtgsub` — wiki-tagged `framexml`, i.e. flagged Blizzard-internal rather than addon-facing — actually callable from addon code?
questions.expect: Unknown; that is the point. If the `framexml` tag means anything enforceable, the lookup is nil or the call errors from an insecure frame. If it is merely documentation of intent, it is a normal function and works.

questions.question: Do `table.freeze`, `table.isfrozen`, `table.removemulti` and `strsplittable` exist at 12.0.7? All four are wiki-listed with ZERO uses in the shipped source, so they rest on Tier 2 alone.
questions.expect: All four present as functions. If any is nil, the wiki list is stale and §5's WoW-additions table needs a correction — which is exactly the failure mode a zero-use, Tier-2-only claim has.

questions.question: Does `issecure()` ever return true in an addon call frame — i.e. can an addon satisfy the `assert(issecure())` guarding `AddLuaErrorHandler`?
questions.expect: false, from a plain addon call frame. Rule 23 currently states the consequence ('no addon may register a Lua error handler this way') as inference from the assert; this measures the premise. Also probe whether AddLuaErrorHandler is even visible to us.
questions.note: NOT DRAINED from the 2026-07-24 run, deliberately. The run recorded issecureResult="errored: false", which is AMBIGUOUS: T_Anatomy.lua used `ok and (res and true or false) or ("errored: "..res)`, and a legitimate `issecure() == false` makes the middle term falsy so Lua's `or` falls through to the ERROR branch. false is the expected answer, so the one result the test exists to record is the one it cannot spell. The expression was fixed 2026-08-05 to branch on `ok` with an if; RE-FLY to get an unambiguous value. The AddLuaErrorHandler=function half was clean but is not on its own worth a KB edit.

questions.question: Do the six `C_CombatLog.*` names that are documented only on `C_CombatLogSecure` (AddEventFilter, ClearEventFilters, GetCurrentEntryInfo, GetCurrentEventInfo, GetEntryCount, ShouldShowCurrentEntry) resolve to nil for an addon?
questions.expect: All six nil on `C_CombatLog` for us — the `Environment = "SecureOnly"` reading. Any that is non-nil means SecureOnly is not enforced by nil-ing the binding, and §3's account of the combat-log surface changes.

questions.question: Does `C_EventUtils.IsCallbackEvent` return true for exactly the 12 `CallbackEvent = true` events? Call it on a flagged event and on a non-flagged one.
questions.expect: true for a flagged event (e.g. MINIMAP_PING), false for an unflagged one (e.g. PLAYER_LOGIN). That would upgrade 'the 12 flagged events are exactly what RegisterEventCallback accepts' from a reasonable reading to a measurement. The function is called nowhere in the shipped Lua, so its behaviour is entirely unexercised.

questions.question: Does `Frame:UnregisterEventCallback` exist, and what is its arity? It has exactly one call site in the whole checkout (FrameUtil.lua:59), no generated doc entry, no wiki page, and is absent from the 12.0.0 added-widget list.
questions.expect: Present as a function on a frame (FrameUtil calls it, so it must be, unless FrameUtil path is dead). Existence is the cheap half; arity needs a call and is recorded as whatever the error says.

questions.question: Do `GetCurrentEventID()` and `GetEventTime(eventProfileIndex)` exist and return anything useful when called from an addon? Neither is called anywhere in the 2298 shipped .lua files, so there is no worked example of obtaining a valid eventProfileIndex.
questions.expect: Both exist (they are in FrameScriptDocumentation). GetCurrentEventID called outside a handler probably returns nil or 0; GetEventTime with that value probably errors or returns nothing. Recording the error IS the answer — it is what tells a future reader the pair is unusable without a profiling CVar.

questions.question: Is `RegisterUnitEvent`'s documented four-unit cap real? The generated docs express the unit parameter as an unbounded variadic; the four-unit limit is Tier 2 only.
questions.expect: Passing 5 units errors, or silently ignores units past the fourth. Distinguish the two: after registering with 5, the test records whether the call raised. If it neither errors nor is observably capped, the Tier-2 cap claim should be softened in §2.2.

questions.question: What does the `SecureHooksAllowed = false` annotation actually do? `hooksecurefunc` a function carrying it (`CreateFromMixins`, `Mixin`) and see whether the hook is refused.
questions.expect: Unknown and genuinely open. The annotation appears in 24 generated doc entries and in zero Lua logic anywhere in the shipped source, and it overlaps the wiki's empirically-derived unhookable list on only ONE name — which is a reason for caution, not confidence. If the hook installs without error, the natural reading ('hooking these raises') is wrong and both §2.4 and module-architecture rule 6 need rewriting.

questions.question: Do the deprecated `UIDropDownMenu_*` globals still resolve for addon code at 12.0.7? UIDropDownMenu.lua opens with `local envTable = GetCurrentEnvironment()` and resolves through `envTable[...]` rather than `_G`.
questions.expect: This is the question `ns.GlobalType` exists for: a name may be absent from `_G` yet present in the addon environment, or vice versa. If `_G.UIDropDownMenu_Initialize` is nil, the file is scoped away from addons and LibUIDropDownMenu's continued use by WeakAurasOptions in 2026 gets a causal explanation the KB currently declines to assert.

questions.question: Does `CreateFromMixins(nil)` error, or silently produce an empty mixin? This is what happens if a .toc lists a mixin file after its consumer.
questions.expect: Errors. The Lua SecureMixin implementation does `for k, v in pairs(mixin)`, which raises on nil — but Mixin/CreateFromMixins are engine functions whose failure mode has never been observed, so the Lua reading may not describe the C one. A silent empty table would be a much nastier failure mode and worth calling out in §1.2.

questions.question: Which of the security primitives are actually visible to an addon? `issecure`, `issecurevariable`, `issecretvalue`, `issecrettable`, `canaccessvalue`, `secureexecuterange`, `forceinsecure`, `hooksecurefunc`, `C_Secrets`. All are absent from the generated docs, and `issecurevariable` appears nowhere in the shipped source either — the wiki is its only source at any tier.
questions.expect: All present as functions (CDMProbe already calls issecretvalue/issecrettable/canaccessvalue successfully). `issecurevariable` is the one to watch: a single Tier-2 source with zero shipped call sites is exactly the shape of a claim that turns out to be stale. This test is also the PRECONDITION for the whole §4.2 table below — if issecretvalue is missing, Secret.lua cannot gate anything.

questions.question: Is the 16-character addon-message prefix limit real, and how is it enforced? Register a 16-char prefix and a 17-char prefix and record both return values.
questions.expect: 16 succeeds, 17 returns false (or errors). The generated docs type the parameter as a bare `cstring` with no limit; wiki (Tier 2) + AceComm's tested comment (Tier 3) agree on 16, which is the strongest corroboration available and still not Tier 1. Harvested from a bare [gap] with no marker — see _meta.status.candidate — and promoted to built because it is pure call-and-record.

questions.question: §4.2 row 1 — store a secret in a local / upvalue / table VALUE.
questions.expect: Allowed. If this errors, nothing else in the table is testable and the whole secret-handling chapter is wrong.

questions.question: §4.2 row 2 — pass a secret to a Lua function.
questions.expect: Allowed. This is the premise of every 'launder it through a helper' pattern.

questions.question: §4.2 row 3 — pass a secret to an unmarked C function (e.g. `strlen`-ish builtin / a C API not marked as secret-accepting).
questions.expect: Errors, unless the API is explicitly marked (§4.5). Which C function is chosen matters: the test uses one with no marking so a pass would be genuinely surprising.

questions.question: §4.2 row 4 — concatenate a secret string/number with `..`.
questions.expect: Allowed, and the RESULT is itself secret. The table says allowed but says nothing about the result's secrecy — record `issecretvalue` on the result, which is the half the KB does not state.

questions.question: §4.2 row 5 — `string.format` / `string.join` / `string.concat` with a secret argument.
questions.expect: Allowed, result secret. Same as above: the secrecy of the OUTPUT is the interesting half, since it decides whether a formatted string can be printed.

questions.question: §4.2 row 6 — arithmetic on a secret number.
questions.expect: Errors. This is the row CDMProbe's HUD is designed around — no cooldown math on a secret.

questions.question: §4.2 row 7 — compare a secret with `==` and with `<`.
questions.expect: Errors. Test BOTH operators separately: `==` on differing types is a plausible engine special case and the table does not distinguish them.

questions.question: §4.2 row 8 — boolean test (`if v then`) on a BOOLEAN secret.
questions.expect: Errors, per Tier 2 — the last unmeasured row of the operation table. The source is `LuaDurationObject:HasExpired(RealTime)`, measured a SECRET BOOLEAN in combat [client 2026-08-06], which is what unblocked this row: it was registered on the grounds that every secret this client hands an addon is a cooldown number, and that is now false. Three preconditions each record `measured = false` with a reason rather than a verdict — nothing on cooldown, a non-boolean return, or a plain return.

questions.question: §4.2 row 9 — boolean test on a NON-boolean secret.
questions.expect: Allowed — type isn't secret, so nil→false and everything else→true. The asymmetry with row 8 is the single subtlest rule in the chapter and the one most likely to be misremembered.

questions.question: §4.2 row 10 — length operator `#` on a secret.
questions.expect: Errors.

questions.question: §4.2 row 11 — use a secret as a table KEY.
questions.expect: Errors. Contrast with row 1 (as a table VALUE, allowed) — the key/value asymmetry is the rule that bites caching code.

questions.question: §4.2 row 12 — index and index-assign a secret (`secret.foo`, `secret["foo"] = 1`).
questions.expect: Both error. Test read and write separately.

questions.question: §4.2 row 13 — call a secret as a function.
questions.expect: Errors.

questions.question: §4.2 row 14 — `type(secret)`.
questions.expect: Allowed and returns the REAL type. This is §4.3's Trap 1: type() passes, then the comparison blows up. Record the returned string — it also tells us what kind of secret the cooldown source hands out.

questions.question: What happens when a Secret Value reaches AceSerializer-3.0 / LibSerialize / LibDeflate? None of the three tests for secrets; AceSerializer's type dispatch ends in `error(MAJOR..": Cannot serialize a value of type '"..t.."'")`.
questions.expect: AceSerializer sees the real type via `type()` (row 14) and takes a normal branch, then errors inside it on a concat/format/length — so the observed failure is a confusing message from the wrong place. Deferred from pass 1 because it needs the three libraries VENDORED into the lab; the §4.2 rows measure the underlying operations first, which is most of the answer.
questions.blocked_on: LibStub loaded

questions.question: Can `RegisterAllEvents` be combined with `UnregisterEvent`? The wiki says no; Blizzard's own Event Trace does exactly that (`self:RegisterAllEvents()` at :107, `self:UnregisterEvent("ADDON_LOADED")` at :702). One of the two is wrong.
questions.expect: Needs a scratch frame plus observation over time — register all, unregister one, count arrivals of that one. Bucket 2.
questions.note: Carries a PAIRED CONTROL (SPELL_UPDATE_USABLE, registered and never unregistered) beside the target. If both read 0 the test returns measured=false — a zero with a dead control proves nothing about unregistration.

questions.question: What do the `SynchronousEvent` / `unique` flags mean? Neither string is documented anywhere reachable — not in the generated docs' Documentation field, not in Blizzard_APIDocumentation, not in Blizzard_EventTrace, and the wiki has no page.
questions.expect: The natural reading (synchronous = dispatched inline; non-synchronous = queued; unique = coalesced to at most one queued instance) is inference, not evidence. Testing it needs firing an event from a known call frame and timestamping the handler — bucket 2, and it may not be reachable from an addon at all.
questions.note: BUILT but it can only ever report measured=false for the flag question, and that is the honest state, not a stub. Two independent blockers: no runtime predicate exposes SynchronousEvent/UniqueEvent the way C_EventUtils.IsCallbackEvent exposes CallbackEvent, so even a positive observation could not be tied to a flag; and no event is raisable from a known call frame without writing client state (SetCVar/LoadAddOn) or a server round trip, where latency is indistinguishable from queueing. What it DOES measure is the C_EventUtils namespace — if a patch ever adds such a predicate, this test finds it.

questions.question: Is `OnUpdate` really blocked by hiding a frame or its parent?
questions.expect: Tier 2 and dated; oUF guards on `self:IsVisible()` independently, which is consistent but not proof. Scratch frame + tick counter across a Hide/Show cycle.

questions.question: Is the leading `_nilOwner` argument to a RegisterEventCallback handler a contract, or six consistent conventions? Is it ever non-nil?
questions.expect: The generated docs declare `EventCallbackType` with NO fields at all, so there is no spec to read. Six shipped call sites all discard a leading arg. Needs registering a callback and inspecting arg 1.

questions.question: Does `ADDONS_UNLOADING` carry `closingClient = false` on a /reload?
questions.expect: Tier 1 supplies only the payload shape; that a reload passes false is inference FROM THE FIELD NAME. Needs a logout/reload observation recorded into SavedVariables — pass 3's journal.

questions.question: What state does a /reload preserve vs discard — is the Lua state fully destroyed or recycled?
questions.expect: No Tier-1 or Tier-2 statement exists. Behaviourally addon chunks re-execute (ADDON_LOADED fires again). Testable by stamping a non-saved global and looking for it after reload — pass 3's journal.

questions.question: What is the real order of PLAYER_LEAVING_WORLD → PLAYER_LOGOUT → ADDONS_UNLOADING, and does it differ on a crash/Alt-F4?
questions.expect: The wiki carries its own {{fact}} tags on both bullets, i.e. it does not vouch for the ordering. Needs the pass-3 journal (record each event with an incrementing sequence number, read it back next session). The crash half is not testable politely.
questions.note: PLAYER_LEAVING_WORLD also fires on every zone change, so early journal lines may be zoning rather than logout. Each line names its own event and carries GetTime(); the tail is the readable part. Deliberately unfiltered — filtering would discard the only evidence of what actually fired. Cannot see a crash or Alt-F4 at all.

questions.question: Does `CreateFontString` accept a fourth `subLevel` argument, or is it silently discarded? Blizzard's own pool code passes four against a documented three-arg signature.
questions.expect: Create two FontStrings on the same frame and draw layer with different subLevel values and see whether stacking order differs. Bucket 2.

questions.question: What does frameStrata `PARENT` actually do? It is the XSD default and is never written explicitly anywhere in the shipped corpus.
questions.expect: Tier 1 gives the value and the default and nothing more. The dropped gloss ('inherit from parent, not a z-band') was inference from the name.

questions.question: Do frame levels run 0–10000, does a child default to one level above its parent, and does moving a parent below 0 clamp to 10000?
questions.expect: All three are Tier 2 only. Cheap once a scratch frame exists — create parent/child, read GetFrameLevel, then SetFrameLevel(0) on the parent and re-read.

questions.question: Is the XSD's listing order of the five draw layers actually the z-order, and does HIGHLIGHT have special mouse-over semantics?
questions.expect: Universally believed, matches the names, and stated at Tier 1 nowhere. Needs two overlapping textures and a visual read — the one pass-1 bucket that a SavedVariables record cannot capture on its own.
questions.note: ANSWERED by eyeball 2026-08-05: OVERLAY draws in front of ARTWORK. ⚠ Five verdicts are on record and they disagree — the first four are from v0.2.0, whose pooled verdict buttons kept a closure over the FIRST question's def and so recorded every answer against this id regardless of which question was on screen (fixed in v0.2.1). Latest-wins gives the correct verdict; the `asked` field recorded beside each verdict is what exposed the mis-binding. Only the ARTWORK/OVERLAY pair was shown, so the full five-way order is still inference from one adjacent pair.

questions.question: Are SetTexture / SetAtlas / SetColorTexture mutually exclusive — does exactly one 'win'? `SetTexture(...)` then `SetAtlas(...)`, read GetTexture()/GetAtlas(), then the reverse order.
questions.expect: The near-universal mental model, consistent with GetTexture returning nil after SetAtlas, and cited at no tier.

questions.question: Do SetVertexColor and SetGradient write the same storage? White 8x8 texture, SetVertexColor(1,0,0), SetGradient(HORIZONTAL, yellow, blue), GetVertexColor(); then reverse.
questions.expect: README §6 calls this the most consequential unresolved gap in the whole subtree, and the workspace has already observed it once — todo/addon-engineering.md records that SetGradient RESETS the vertex colour to white. That prior observation makes this a confirm-and-cite, not a discovery.

questions.question: Do FontString:SetTextColor and Region:GetVertexColor share storage? `fs:SetTextColor(1,0,0)` then `fs:GetVertexColor()`, and the reverse.
questions.expect: 'Identical annotations ⇒ identical storage' is inference. The two wiki pages say nothing about the relationship, and one of them was effectively abandoned in 2021.

questions.question: What does an alpha or vertex-colour animation do to the underlying value when it stops WITHOUT `setToFinalAlpha`?
questions.expect: The attribute's existence implies restoration, but that is inference and is stated at no tier. Needs an AnimationGroup and a read after OnFinished.
questions.note: Needs TWO runs. The Stop-path numbers land on the first; the natural-finish numbers come from a persistent arm whose OnFinished fires after `run` has already returned, so a later run reads them. Until then it reports finishMeasured=false with a why — never a stand-in value.

questions.question: Does an XML `<OnLoad>` body receive the addon-table varargs? Of 2123 shipped `<OnLoad` occurrences, 6 have `...` nearby and all six forward event/callback varargs — but that is four distinct sites, one of them dead code.
questions.expect: An argument from silence, not evidence; the KB explicitly declines to assume either way. Needs the lab to ship an XML file.

questions.question: Do the ASPECT-LESS secret sinks actually move a pixel? `Texture:SetAtlas` and `AnimVertexColor:SetStartColor`/`SetEndColor` accept a Secret Value, declare no `SecretArgumentsAddAspect`, expose no getter, and leave the anchor chain clean — so 'accepted, nothing observable changed' is the strongest statement any instrument can make. Only an eyeball can close it. (`SetTexture` REFUSES and `SetColorTexture` POISONS the anchor chain — both are settled and are NOT part of this question.)
questions.expect: Set each from a known secret whose value is inferable from context (e.g. a boolean-ish count at a threshold), and LOOK. Either the atlas/colour visibly tracks the secret — in which case these are real display channels with no readback, and the KB's channel table gains two rows — or nothing moves, and 'accepted' means the call was silently dropped. ⚠ There is no programmatic oracle by construction: do not build one, and do not accept an INERT verdict as evidence either way.
questions.blocked_on: a secret that is itself a valid atlas name
questions.note: STILL OPEN after a visual check on 2026-08-05, deliberately not drained. The SetAtlas half was shown as three cells (valid name / invalid name / secret string) and the person reported the secret cell INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE INVALID one — so the blankness cannot be attributed to secrecy, because an atlas name is a string and the only secret string obtainable (a concatenation, §4.2 row 4) is never a valid atlas name. The control is what revealed that; without it the run would have looked like a clean negative. Settling SetAtlas needs a secret that is ITSELF a valid atlas name and no such source is known. The AnimVertexColor SetStartColor/SetEndColor half is UNATTEMPTED and is the live one — those take colours, not names, so the category problem does not apply.

questions.question: ⭐ Is `item.auraDataCached` / `item:GetAuraDataCached()` on a Cooldown Manager item frame PLAIN in combat, or secret like every sibling field? Every other aura-derived field on that frame measured secret; this one is unmeasured.
questions.expect: UNKNOWN, and it is the highest-value open question in the subtree. If the record is plain in combat it carries `expirationTime`/`duration`, which makes the in-combat DoT-remaining read that `cooldown-manager.md` §5.1 and §7 BOTH declare unanswerable already available on the frame. Method: `ns.ClassOf` the record itself BEFORE indexing it (the container may be secret independently of its fields, per the 12.1.0 `UNIT_AURA` note), then class-check each field. Needs a real pull with a bound aura — out of combat proves nothing, since every sibling reads fine there too.

questions.question: Is `x == nil` genuinely PERMITTED on a Secret Value, while `x == <number>` throws? Bare `==` against a number killed a refresh loop the instant combat started `[client 2026-08-04]`, but nil-guards have run on secrets every sample of every capture without raising.
questions.expect: The asymmetry is consistent with the model — comparing to nil leaks nothing not already knowable — but it is inferred from two data points and NO Tier-1 statement says so. Test both directions against a known secret inside `pcall`: `s == nil`, `nil == s`, `s ~= nil`, and a control `s == 0` that must throw. ⚠ A pass does NOT license comparing to nil in product code — house rule stands: class-check first, branch on the class. This question exists to make the KB's claim honest, not to change the practice.

questions.question: Does `TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED` fire on a HERO-TREE swap (which changes the build without changing the spec), and how many times per loadout swap? `PLAYER_SPECIALIZATION_CHANGED` demonstrably does not, so a hero-tree cache keyed to it goes stale.
questions.expect: Reasoned from the event's purpose, NOT observed — that is why it is here. Register both events plus `TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED`, log every firing with `C_ClassTalents.GetActiveHeroTalentSpec()` beside it, then swap hero tree without swapping spec. Expect TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED n>1 and PLAYER_SPECIALIZATION_CHANGED n=0. The COUNT matters as much as the fact: anything it triggers must be idempotent and must not re-announce an unchanged answer. ⚠ Anchor is outside knowledge/addon-dev/ — the finding is parked in the game KB's inbox because it has no home topic file yet (that placement is itself an open KB-structure call).
questions.note: Observational: an always-on listener installed at file load tallies PER-EVENT counts, so a reading requires an actual hero-tree swap during the session. A zero count reports measured=false, never 'it does not fire'.

questions.question: Does the CDM item frame's PLAIN `auraInstanceID` reach `C_UnitAuras.GetAuraDuration`, yielding a `LuaDurationObject` that carries the sealed aura timing for display? Measured on a BUFF row and a DEBUFF row separately.
questions.expect: UNKNOWN, and it is the follow-on to `cdm-auradatacached-plain-in-combat`. That measurement killed the direct read (`expirationTime`/`duration`/`timeMod`/`applications` all secret) but left `auraInstanceID` PLAIN — and a secret can never be fed INTO a curve or a duration, since every sink is `AllowedWhenUntainted` and all four negative controls refused `[client 2026-08-04]`. The sanctioned route is the reverse: an API returns an object already carrying the secret internally. §4.8.1 measured `C_UnitAuras.GetAuraDuration` behaving identically to `GetSpellCooldownDuration`, so IF the plain instance id is the key it accepts, the CDM frame supplies a legal in-combat aura timer for display — which is a capability, not a footnote. ⚠ The SIGNATURE is unverified: both arities are tried and the error is recorded, because an argument-count complaint names the real shape. ⚠ `HasSecretValues()` is `ReturnsNeverSecret`, so its VALUE (not just its class) is the one real readback — expect true in combat. ⚠ `GetRemainingDuration` returning a PLAIN number in combat would be a hole in the seal, not a convenience; do not treat it as one. ⚠ The duration sinks are ASPECT-LESS, so this test can prove the object was obtained and carries secrets, and can NEVER prove a pixel moved — that half needs an eyeball.
questions.note: Destruction is the target spec: it puts a DoT on the target (Immolate 133441 / Wither 164597 -> auraDataUnit "target") and carries player-side buffs (Backdraft, Malevolence, Conflagration of Chaos -> "player"), so one dummy pull exercises both sides. Rows are bucketed by `auraDataUnit`, never by spell id, so the split stays spec-agnostic.

questions.question: Does a secret-bearing aura duration obtained via `C_UnitAuras.GetAuraDuration` actually DRAW when fed to `StatusBar:SetTimerDuration` — for a player buff and a target debuff alike?
questions.expect: UNKNOWN, and unknowable by instrument: all three duration sinks declare NO `SecretArgumentsAddAspect`, so there is no readback of any kind and 'the call was accepted' is not evidence a pixel moved. §4.8.1 states it outright — on an aspect-less channel the only oracle is an eyeball. `cdm-aura-duration-object-chain` already proved the object is obtained on both sides and that `HasSecretValues()` is true, so what is left is purely whether it renders. ⚠ A PLAIN CONTROL duration is shown in the same frame: without it 'the bar is empty' cannot be told from 'this widget never animates'. ⚠ `SetMinMaxValues(0,1)` is called BEFORE the timer on every bar — the known trap is a correctly installed duration drawing at 0 % width, which would read as the secret having been dropped. ⚠ 'control doesn't animate either' is a real option and indicts the STIMULUS, not the channel.
questions.note: VISUAL CHECK (ns.Ask.Register), no ns.Test — by construction there is no programmatic oracle. Needs a live bound aura in combat; the stimulus refuses to draw and says so when none is present, rather than showing empty bars that could be answered by mistake. Destruction gives both sides at once (Immolate on the target, a self-buff on the player).

questions.question: Does C_AssistedCombat.GetNextCastSpell's return VARY over a pull, or is it constant? §7 proves it is readable in combat but recorded a constant 691 (Summon Felhunter) at every sample.
questions.expect: UNKNOWN, and the instrument is the point. The 691 constant is NOT evidence the oracle is stuck: the recorder that produced it dedups by readability CLASS, so it sampled only at readable⇄secret transitions — of which there were none — and a value changing every GCD would have been recorded exactly once, indistinguishable from one that never changed. This samples on the player's own UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED instead, one sample per GCD boundary, paired with the cast that preceded it. distinctValues == 1 across a real pull means the oracle is constant and projects/combat-assist spec §3.1 has no content — that would kill M3 and force §6's first open question immediately. distinctValues > 1 means it moves, and whether it moves SENSIBLY is a judgement for a human reading the series, not for this test.

questions.question: Can `item.cooldownID` on a Cooldown Manager item frame read SECRET, and in which state? Measured on the FIELD and on the accessor `item:GetCooldownID()` — the KB row names the field, a consumer calls the accessor, and they are not the same expression.
questions.expect: UNKNOWN. It is the only untagged row in a §7 Tier 2 table whose twelve neighbours all carry `[client]`, and it is load-bearing: `resolve out of combat, never overwrite a known-good id with an unreadable one` is the whole merge-don't-replace design of anything binding to the CDM. A result showing it is never secret does not fail the milestone — it means that machinery is unreachable and should be simplified rather than kept because it was expensive to write. ⚠ This row deliberately does NOT declare needs="secret": that gate records `skipped` out of combat, `skipped` never drains, and the out-of-combat half IS half the claim — gating it would lose that half by construction.
questions.note: Returns `{ooc = {...}, combat = {...}}`, with `partial = true` while only the OOC half is on record — `partial` sorts below a complete result at drain time without refusing it. Ever-secret accumulates as a max rather than being replaced: one sighting answers `can read secret`, and a later all-plain sample must not erase it. The test also samples itself every 3 s through a pull, because one reading 2 s in is a weak reading of a field that can only go secret while something is rolling.

questions.question: Does `CooldownViewerMixin:GetItemFrames()` still return item frames when the viewer itself is HIDDEN?
questions.expect: Tier 1 PREDICTS the children survive, and that is the reason to measure it rather than to assume it. GetItemFrames is GetLayoutChildren (`CooldownViewer.lua:1490-1497`), whose filter tests each CHILD's own `IsShown()` plus a `layoutIndex` (`LayoutFrame.lua:38`) rather than the viewer's `IsVisible()`, and the viewer's `OnHide` unregisters events without releasing `itemFramePool` (`:1570-1580`). It decides whether a consumer's `hidden` and `empty` health verdicts can discriminate at all, or should collapse to one. ⚠ FIVE NUMBERS OR IT PRODUCES A FALSE ANSWER — an empty list has three incompatible causes (the IsShown filter dropped every child / the pool holds nothing / no child carries a layoutIndex), so each row records IsShown, IsVisible, the raw child count, the pool-active count, #GetItemFrames() and how many raw children individually pass IsShown().
questions.note: Observational, and it declines rather than hiding a Blizzard frame itself — hiding a protected, Edit-Mode-managed frame from an addon is a different question with worse consequences. The precondition is a viewer that is hidden AND still holds pooled item frames; hidden-and-empty answers nothing and is reported as such. ⚠ The OOC pass fires only at PLAYER_LOGIN (+6 s) and on a spec/hero swap, so hiding a viewer mid-session produces no new run unless you press `/clab -> run all tests` or /reload.

questions.question: Is an ordinary addon frame parented and anchored to UIParent `IsProtected() == false`, does anchoring it to a protected Blizzard frame change that, and do SetPoint / SetScale / Show / Hide still succeed on it IN COMBAT?
questions.expect: §1.1 asserts the frame is unprotected; §1.2 states that protection propagates to a protected frame's parents and anchor targets. But UIParent is itself `protected="true"`, so a child of UIParent anchored to UIParent sits beside both legs of that rule, and the resolution — that the spread runs upward/outward FROM the protected frame and leaves such a child alone — is stated nowhere. Everything an addon draws rests on it. The in-combat pcalls are the half the claim is actually cashed for: all four setters sit in the protected-widget 59, and a `UI_SCALE_CHANGED` handler that re-`SetPoint`s carries no combat guard. Free rider: `:183`'s `[unverified]` on IsProtected()'s SECOND return is settled by recording both returns.
questions.note: No needs="secret" — nothing here involves secret values and the gate would record `skipped` out of combat, where half the reading is taken. The protected anchor target is VERIFIED rather than assumed: the candidate's own IsProtected() is recorded beside it, and if no candidate reports itself protected the §1.2 half says so rather than implying a negative. Frames are created once at load; `run` executes on every retry tick.

questions.question: Does `SetClampedToScreen(true)` re-clamp a frame parked past a screen edge when its own geometry changes (SetScale) or the screen's does (UI_SCALE_CHANGED / DISPLAY_SIZE_CHANGED), or is the clamp applied once at the call?
questions.expect: UNKNOWN — Tier 1 declares the setter and says nothing about when it applies. The case that matters is a movable panel parked at an edge and then met by a resolution or UI-scale change: a one-shot clamp walks the panel off screen with no recovery but a position reset. ⚠ Three ways to read a wrong number, all designed against: `GetLeft()` is in the frame's OWN coordinate space, so every reading is converted to screen units and compared against UIParent's equivalent (otherwise SetScale 'measures' a clamp failure that is arithmetic); the C layer plausibly applies the clamp off-frame, so each step is read inline AND after a settle; and `run` executes on every retry tick, so the frame is created once at load, kept shown but empty so a hidden frame is not a fourth confounder.
questions.note: The screen-side half is deliberately NOT `blocked` — a UI-scale change is one slider away, so the test declines with an instruction (`move the UI Scale slider, or /console uiScale 0.85`) and clears itself. `blocked` is for an input that does not exist on this machine and would drop the row out of coverage forever.

questions.question: §4.8 — does LuaDurationObject:HasExpired / IsActive / HasStarted / IsZero return a PLAIN boolean in restricted combat? None carries a secrecy annotation, but neither does GetRemainingDuration, which IS measured secret.
questions.expect: UNKNOWN, and the annotation is not evidence either way. §4.8's roster lists these four predicates with no SecretWhen* and no ReturnsNeverSecret — exactly the annotation state of GetRemainingDuration, which finding 7 measured SECRET in combat. So absence of a marker is known NOT to be a guarantee on this object. Three outcomes, all useful to projects/combat-assist: a PLAIN boolean makes ready(this) one exact call and deletes the readiness latch that 6 of 9 Demonology catalog entries depend on; a SECRET boolean still drives emphasis leak-free through SetVertexColorFromBoolean / SetAlphaFromBoolean (both AllowedWhenTainted with SecretArgumentsAddAspect) but may never gate a band condition; a raise means the route does not exist. HasSecretValues() is ReturnsNeverSecret and is the GATE — a duration holding nothing secret proves nothing, so the test refuses to answer until it finds one that does, and GetRemainingDuration runs as the control.

questions.question: In COMBAT, can a consumer read a row's current DISPLAY identity — via item:GetSpellID() or via GetCooldownViewerCooldownInfo(cid).overrideSpellID? GetSpellID is measured secret on aura-bound rows; the info struct has never been read in combat at all.
questions.expect: UNKNOWN, and the two candidate routes carry opposite evidence. item:GetSpellID() was measured secret on 8 of 51 rows and those 8 were exactly the rows carrying a live bound aura — so a row with NO bound aura may survive, but that was never measured separately. GetCooldownViewerCooldownInfo is Tier-1 documented as structural config 'readable even when live state is not', yet every reading of it on record was taken out of combat, including cap's own 200-row v0.2.0 capture. Splitting each row by auraDataUnit is the measurement: if secrecy tracks aura-boundness, a non-aura row is a working in-combat identity route. This gates projects/combat-assist catalog entry E6 (Ruination), whose whole content is a mid-combat transform — Bind refuses to resolve in combat, so without an independent read E6 is dead code that would pass every unit test and never light once in play.

questions.question: For a LuaCurveObject with points (0,10) and (20,20): what does Step snap to between them, and what do Linear and Step return OUTSIDE the point range?
questions.expect: UNKNOWN on both cells, and NEITHER needs a secret — curve semantics are a property of the curve, so plain inputs settle them and this answers out of combat on the first run. STEP DIRECTION: the docs say 'performs no interpolation between points, instead snapping to values exactly' without saying WHICH point. Previous-point-hold and nearest-point are both consistent and put a threshold in different places — with points at 0 and 20, hold gives an edge at 20, nearest gives one at 10. Read y at x=9.9 / 10 / 10.1 to separate them. OUT-OF-RANGE: clamping is INFERRED and never documented — Blizzard's EncounterTimelineTrailAlphaCurve defines points only at x=0.0 and x=0.1 yet drives alpha across a full 0..1 progress, which only works if x>0.1 clamps to the last y. x=-5 and x=100 settle it. Nothing in the shipped UI uses Step at all, so there is no precedent to read either off. Gates whether projects/combat-assist may threshold a cooldown with a Step curve or must pad a Linear one.

questions.question: §4.8.4 — with a NON-secret curve, does LuaDurationObject:Evaluate*(curve, modifier) return a plain number in restricted combat? `SecretWhenCurveSecret` read literally says yes, which would be a leak.
questions.expect: UNKNOWN, and the annotation is the whole problem. All five Evaluate* methods carry `SecretWhenCurveSecret` — secret WHEN THE CURVE IS — and ours is not. Read literally that returns a READABLE number derived from a duration measured SECRET on the same object (§4.8.4, GetRemainingDuration), which would let a caller binary-search the remaining time. Either the annotation is incomplete or it is a leak; §4.8.4 records the cell as unmeasured rather than guessing. The curve is an identity over 0..600 so a PLAIN result is legible as the remaining time itself rather than as an opaque number. `HasSecretValues()` on the DURATION is the gate — an unrestricted duration proves nothing — and GetRemainingDuration is the control; if the control reads plain the object is not restricted and every other cell is meaningless. A table result is checked at a MEMBER, since a colour result is a readable table with secret members (§4.8.1 finding 9). The answer decides what an addon may DO with the result, not whether the route works: SetDesaturation and SetVertexColor take a secret either way. PLAIN is the finding that matters — it means the graded emphasis route hands Lua a value the restriction exists to withhold, which is a legitimacy problem for projects/combat-assist §5 rather than a technical one.

questions.question: Of the 59 `IsProtectedFunction = true` widget methods, only `SetPoint` / `SetScale` / `Show` / `Hide` were exercised IN COMBAT on an ordinary addon frame. Do the other 55 also succeed there — `SetFrameStrata` and `SetHeight`/`SetWidth` above all?
questions.expect: All 55 succeed, because the frame reads `IsProtected() == false` and protection is what the restriction keys on — but that is an INFERENCE from four calls plus one predicate, and §1.1's general claim is currently cashed for more than it measured. `SetFrameStrata` is the one worth its own verdict: it is additionally the only `SecretArguments = NotAllowed` member of the strata/level family (`frames-textures-animation.md` §4.2), so it has a second reason to behave differently and no measurement either way. Method: one plain `CreateFrame("Frame", nil, UIParent)`, each of the 55 called under `pcall` in combat, recording the raised message rather than a boolean — an error's TEXT is what distinguishes 'protected-function refusal' from 'bad argument'. ⚠ Calls that change what is on screen (SetParent, Show/Hide chains) must run on a throwaway frame, not on anything the lab draws.
questions.note: Registered because `projects/combat-assist` is BUILDING on the four-call half: `Overlay.lua` keeps `SetFrameStrata` out of combat deliberately and confines its in-combat writes to Show/Hide/SetVertexColor/SetAlpha, citing this marker. That is the marker doing its job — the code routed around the unknown rather than assuming it — so the question is recorded, not queued.

questions.question: Does an addon frame ANCHORED to a frame carrying a SECRET anchor still accept `SetPoint` / `Show` / `Hide` in combat? The measured case anchored to `ActionButton1`, which is protected but is never fed a secret; a CDM item frame in combat is fed one.
questions.expect: UNKNOWN, and the two halves are genuinely different questions. §4.8.1 findings 10 and 12 record anchor-chain contagion propagating DOWN to the dependent from `FontString:SetText` and `Texture:SetColorTexture`, and the Cooldown Manager writes secret cooldown text onto its own item frames in combat — so the route exists and nothing has been executed along it. Method: an ordinary UIParent-parented frame anchored to a live CDM item frame, then in combat `SetPoint` it to a KNOWN-DIFFERENT offset and read `GetLeft()` back, converted to screen units. ⚠ A `pcall` that does not raise is NOT the measurement — the failure mode this question exists for is a geometry write that silently no-ops, so the readback is the whole test and a test that only records 'no error' would manufacture a false pass.
questions.note: Registered because `projects/combat-assist`'s overlay is exactly this shape — UIParent-parented, anchored to a CDM item frame, re-anchored mid-pull when the item-frame pool recycles. Its M3c acceptance table now names this gap as the reading for 'overlay visibly on the wrong icon after a repool', so the unknown is surfaced where a flight would meet it rather than tested.

questions.question: Does `item.auraDataUnit` on a CDM item frame supply the right `unit` alongside the same frame's `auraInstanceID` for `C_UnitAuras.GetAuraApplicationDisplayCount` — on a TARGET aura as well as a player one?
questions.expect: It pairs, because both fields describe the same bound aura on the same frame and `auraDataUnit` is non-nil iff there is one. But that is a COMPOSITION of two separately measured facts and has never been run as a pair: the flown quantiser cue hardcoded `"player"`, which is correct for a self-buff and says nothing about a target aura. Method: read both fields off one frame and pass them together, on a row bound to a target debuff (Destruction's Immolate gives one) and on a player buff in the same pull. ⚠ The quantiser has NO READBACK — an empty string is what 'below the threshold' looks like as well as what a wrong unit would look like — so the oracle is an eyeball on a count that is known to be above the threshold, never the call's return.
questions.note: The old planned CAP route is obsolete on 12.1: aura instance IDs are secret and the sanctioned AuraContainer replacement was accepted by `aura-container-backdraft-stack-cue`. Keep this parked only for legacy composition evidence.

questions.question: Can a spell-ID-filtered 12.1 AuraContainer slot show a useful Backdraft context tile in restricted combat: icon and aura-duration swipe at one stack, no numeric count below two, then the client-produced count 2 at two stacks?
questions.expect: The tile appears when Backdraft is present, its duration swipe advances without addon Lua reading a duration, the application-count FontString is empty at one stack, and it displays 2 at two stacks. This is a visual question by construction: the AuraButton becomes forbidden while its AuraData is secret and IsShown is itself secret, so the test must not inspect the button, FontString text, visibility, or Cooldown after registration. A human verdict is the only oracle. Setup declares includeSpellIDs[117828], unit player, and registers SetIcon, SetDurationCooldown, and SetApplicationCount sinks during initializeFrame.
questions.note: Open the visual-check panel out of combat as Destruction, enter combat, and cast Conflagrate from zero Backdraft through one and two stacks. Leave combat before choosing the verdict so the panel can retire the formerly restricted stimulus safely. This gates Combat Assist Phase 9's sealed context cue and replaces the pre-12.1 auraInstanceID plan.

questions.question: Which C_Spell.GetSpellCharges(17962) members remain readable in restricted combat, and does its NeverSecret isActive member distinguish Conflagrate at 2/2, 1/2, and 0/2 charges?
questions.expect: The returned table remains indexable; currentCharges, cooldownStartTime, cooldownDuration, and chargeModRate become secret in combat; maxCharges remains plain 2; isActive remains plain, false at 2/2 and true at both 1/2 and 0/2. That result would prove isActive describes whether recharge is running, exactly as the Tier-1 documentation says, and cannot replace a charged-readiness estimator because it does not distinguish castable 1/2 from uncastable 0/2. Any plain currentCharges result would remove the napkin entirely and must be treated as the important contrary finding.
questions.note: Start Destruction with Conflagrate exactly 2/2, reload, enter combat, then cast it twice quickly. The probe samples the direct spell API at the seed, combat entry, and after each successful cast. It never enumerates, hooks, retains, or reads a Cooldown Manager frame.

questions.question: Do the exact Conflagrate display count and a client-owned next-charge swipe render during restricted combat, and can ordinary styling visibly reverse and recolor that swipe?
questions.expect: At 2/2 the count shows 2 and the recharge swipes are clear. After each cast the exact count changes to 1 then 0 without addon readback. Both swipes track the next individual recharge; the right one is visibly teal and reversed. When the first charge returns the count becomes 1 and both duration-object swipes reset to the next active recharge. The probe uses GetSpellDisplayCount directly into FontString:SetText and GetSpellChargeDuration directly into two Cooldown:SetCooldownFromDurationObject sinks; it owns no timer and never reads a secret back.
questions.note: Open the visual-check panel out of combat as Destruction at exactly 2/2 Conflagrate. Enter combat, cast twice, and watch through one natural recharge. The single short verdict is only whether all three columns worked; report which column failed in chat if not. This tests presentation only and does not replace the separate finding that Lua cannot branch on exact count.

questions.question: Is the item's Cooldown widget IsShown() a plain boolean in restricted combat, and does wasSetFromCooldown stay plain beside it?
questions.expect: Both plain on every laid-out Essential row, in and out of combat: `shown` tallies only true/false (never secret/threw), and `wasSetFromCooldown` likewise. That combination makes `IsShown() and wasSetFromCooldown` a legal in-combat gate for 'this row's own cooldown is running'. A `secret` or `threw` in either tally kills the gate and cap falls back to the alert latch, which is known one-way.
questions.note: The tab-2 sibling Bar.Pip:IsShown() is already measured plain in combat, which is why this is expected to pass — but Pip is a different widget on a different mixin and the inference is exactly what needs checking. Run in a pull with several abilities on cooldown so both states appear.

questions.question: Does OnCooldownDone on the item's Cooldown widget fire for rows the player configured no alert on — the symmetric ready edge the alert channel cannot give us?
questions.expect: doneDistinctRows well above the number of rows carrying a configured alert, ideally every row that came off cooldown during the pull. The 2026-08-16 flight measured Available on exactly ONE cooldownID out of nine; if doneDistinctRows reaches most of the nine, OnCooldownDone is the symmetric edge and the asymmetry is an alert-system property rather than a client one. doneFirings 0 after a real pull would falsify the whole route.
questions.note: The hook cannot report the pull that installed it, so the first run arms and returns measured=false; a later run in the same session reports. Compare doneFirings against alertFirings in the same payload.

questions.question: Are isOnActualCooldown, cooldownIsActive, isOnGCD and the method IsOnCooldown() plain in restricted combat?
questions.expect: Unknown, and genuinely open. They derive from spellCooldownInfo.endTime, which is secret in combat, so `cooldownIsActive = endTime > timeNow` may well hand tainted code a secret boolean — or Blizzard's untainted comparison may yield a plain one. If any is plain it is a strictly simpler answer than the widget-state gate, being Blizzard's own verdict rather than a mirror of it.
questions.note: Cheap: rides the same row walk as the other reads. The interesting cell is IsOnCooldown() — a method, so it can also THROW on a secret comparison, which is itself the finding.

questions.question: Feeding a duration object into a hidden scratch Cooldown widget and reading IsShown() — is that a plain boolean when the underlying time is secret?
questions.expect: Plain true/false per row. §2.3 documents this as a working secret-safe yes/no, but that is another addon's claim mined into the KB and never measured here; it is currently load-bearing for nothing, and would become a general-purpose 'is any duration running' primitive if it holds. Note the standing hazard the section names: GetCooldownTimes() goes secret after SetCooldownFromDurationObject, so never scrape times back off the widget.
questions.note: Independent of the CDM item frames — it only needs a spellID and C_Spell.GetSpellCooldownDuration, so it answers even if the viewer is empty.

questions.question: Does calling viewer:RegisterItemFrameForOnUpdate(item) from addon code make Available fire for a row with no configured alert, without writing the player's saved layout or playing an alert?
questions.expect: registeredAfter equals the row count and hasOnUpdateScript true. Because alertsByEvent stays empty, TriggerAlertEvent should still be CALLED (so a hooksecurefunc observer sees the edge) while playing no sound or text. The open half is durability: RefreshOnUpdateRegistration runs on several paths and will un-register a row whose alertsByEvent is empty, so a second run some time later should show whether the registration survived.
questions.note: Deliberately NOT the route cap took — OnCooldownDone needs no registration at all. Measured because it is the obvious alternative and someone will propose it again. Out of combat only: UpdateOnUpdateScript does a SetScript on the viewer.
questions.blocked_on: it WRITES to the viewer: RegisterItemFrameForOnUpdate mutates itemFramesNeedingOnUpdateMap and UpdateOnUpdateScript does a SetScript on the viewer, both from tainted code. That is the same class of thing CDMSweep/Cue/Glow were retired from the 12.1 lab for. Not worth the risk to measure a route we already decided against (OnCooldownDone needs no registration). Unpark only with a deliberate decision.

questions.question: Is a laid-out CDM item frame PROTECTED at runtime, in and out of combat?
questions.expect: Unknown. The XML declares no protected attribute across Blizzard_CooldownViewer, but that settles the declaration and not the runtime, and 12.1.0 added a CooldownViewerSecure.lua nobody has read. If IsProtected() returns false in combat, cap may re-anchor rows mid-pull and the whole RefreshLayout-teardown risk becomes recoverable in place; if true, the out-of-combat-only guard in Anchor.lua is load-bearing rather than cautious.
questions.note: Long-open: it has been the last item of the CDM-positioning work since the anchor probe was written. Reports both the item frames and the viewer, since a secure ancestor is one of the routes by which a frame becomes protected without declaring it.
